question: For the 185 NSW-treated men in the Dehejia-Wahba subsample, what is the average effect of the training program on 1978 earnings (ATT, 1982 dollars) estimated against the CPS-1 non-experimental comparison group under selection on observables, using an estimator fixed by a rule from outside this literature, and how does it compare with the experimental benchmark of $1,794 (SE 633; Dehejia and Wahba 1999, Table 3)?
hypotheses: H1: The pre-specified ATT on 1978 earnings is positive, with a 95% confidence interval that excludes zero. If H3 fails, H1's result is reported as a statistical contrast between groups, not as a causal effect.

H2 (descriptive, not a test): the difference between the pre-specified estimate and the benchmark, with an approximate combined standard error that ignores the shared treated units (so it overstates the uncertainty), is reported; closeness to the benchmark is never used to choose or rank estimators.

H3 (placebo that can fail): the same estimator applied to 1975 earnings as the outcome, without conditioning on 1975 earnings or 1975 unemployment, gives a 95% confidence interval that includes zero. The literature predicts this fails (Imbens and Xu 2025).
contribution: A pre-committed replication of a well-studied benchmark-recovery exercise. The crew had read the published estimates on this sample, including which estimators land near the benchmark, so the commitment is not blind to the literature: what it rules out is outcome search within this study. To limit the influence of the literature, the primary estimator is fixed by a rule from outside it: the cross-fitted AIPW ATT estimator already pre-specified for the crew's ss-null-effect seed, applied unchanged apart from the covariate set. The estimate itself is not new, and the paper says so.

tasks.title: Literature on recovering the NSW benchmark from observational comparison groups; the benchmark itself and its source

design_constraints: Estimand: the ATT for all 185 DW-treated men. Any overlap trimming removes comparison (CPS) units only, never treated units.

Primary estimator: the cross-fitted AIPW ATT estimator of gallery/ss-null-effect (its plan.json design.method), applied unchanged apart from the covariate set; any unavoidable adaptation is listed as a deviation.
RE78 is set aside before any data-prep run: data-prep writes a working file without RE78, and RE78 is joined back only by the first analysis run after the design gate.
Benchmark: $1,794 (SE 633), Dehejia and Wahba (1999), Table 3, row NSW, column (1).
